## Getting Details for a Particular IP Address Range

To get details for a particular IP address range:

1. Send a `GET` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/v2/ipRanges/{ipRangeId}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/72057594037927936/v2/ipRanges/72057594038636775`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `ipRangeId`: The unique identifier of the IP address range.

- View an example response

```
{
  "id": "72057594038636775",
  "modifiedTime": "1675179304",
  "creationTime": "1675178886",
  "modifiedBy": "72057594037957297",
  "isDeleted": "0",
  "customerId": "72057594037927936",
  "name": "Example IP Address Range",
  "description": "s",
  "ipRangeBegin": "10.1.1.1",
  "ipRangeEnd": "10.1.1.40",
  "latitudeInDb": "28.7040592",
  "longitudeInDb": "77.10249019999999",
  "location": "Delhi, India",
  "countryCode": "IN",
  "enabled": true,
  "totalIps": "40",
  "sccmFlag": false
}
```

A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Adding a New IP Address Range

To add a new IP address range:

1. Send a `POST` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/v2/ipRanges`.
2. Provide the `customerId`, the ZPA tenant ID of the customer, in the request endpoint. For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/72057594037927936/v2/ipRanges`.
3. Include the request headers to provide information about the request context:
  - Content-Type: `application/json`
  - Authorization: Bearer `<access_token>`
4. Use the following JSON payload and provide the following:
  - `name`: The name of IP address range.
  - `ipRangeBegin`: The beginning IP address range. The beginning IP address range must be less than the ending IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed.
  - `ipRangeEnd`: The ending IP address range. The ending IP address range must be greater than the beginning IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed.
  - `subnetCidr`: The IP address subnet in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation used for server-to-client connectivity. The `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are not required if `subnetCidr` is passed.
  - `location`: The location of the IP address range.
  - `latitudeInDb`: The latitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range.
  - `longitudeInDb`: The longitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range.
  - `sccmFlag`: Indicates if the location hint is sent along with a Zscaler IP address to Zscaler Client Connector if it is configured. If Zscaler Client Connector receives the location hint, Zscaler Client Connector creates a pseudo network adapter and applies the location hint to the name of the adapter for the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) location boundary.
  - `enabled`: Indicates if the IP address range is enabled (`true`) or disabled (`false`).

- View the JSON payload

```
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ipRangeBegin": "string",
  "ipRangeEnd": "string",
  "subnetCidr": "string",
  "latitudeInDb": "string",
  "longitudeInDb": "string",
  "location": "string",
  "countryCode": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "sccmFlag": true,
  "locationHint": "string"
}
```

- View an example JSON payload

```
{
   "name":"Example IP Address Range",
   "enabled":true,
   "ipRangeBegin":"194.158.10.0",
   "ipRangeEnd":"194.158.15.0",
   "description":"Example Description",
   "sccmFlag":false,
   "latitudeInDb":37.7749295,
   "longitudeInDb":-122.4194155,
   "countryCode":"US",
   "location":"San Francisco, CA, USA"
}
```

- View an example response

```
{
    "id": "72057594038900885",
    "modifiedTime": "1752776656",
    "creationTime": "1752776656",
    "modifiedBy": "72057594038040687",
    "isDeleted": "0",
    "customerId": "72057594037927936",
    "name": "Example IP Address Range",
    "description": "Example Description",
    "ipRangeBegin": "194.158.10.0",
    "ipRangeEnd": "194.158.15.0",

    "sccmFlag": false
}
```

A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Updating an IP Address Range

To update an existing IP address range:

1. Send a `PUT` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/v2/ipRanges/{ipRangeId}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/72057594037927936/v2/ipRanges/72057594038636775`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `ipRangeId`: The unique identifier of the IP address range.
3. Include the request headers to provide information about the request context:
  - Content-Type: `application/json`
  - Authorization: Bearer `<access_token>`
4. Use the following JSON payload and provide the following:
  - `name`: The name of IP address range.
  - `ipRangeBegin`: The beginning IP address range. The beginning IP address range must be less than the ending IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed.
  - `ipRangeEnd`: The ending IP address range. The ending IP address range must be greater than the beginning IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed.
  - `subnetCidr`: The IP address subnet in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation used for server-to-client connectivity. The `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are not required if `subnetCidr` is passed.
  - `location`: The location of the IP address range.
  - `latitudeInDb`: The latitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range.
  - `longitudeInDb`: The longitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range.
  - `sccmFlag`: Indicates if the location hint is sent along with a Zscaler IP address to Zscaler Client Connector if it is configured. If Zscaler Client Connector receives the location hint, Zscaler Client Connector creates a pseudo network adapter and applies the location hint to the name of the adapter for the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) location boundary.
  - `enabled`: Indicates if the IP address range is enabled (`true`) or disabled (`false`).

- View the example JSON payload

```
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ipRangeBegin": "string",
  "ipRangeEnd": "string",
  "subnetCidr": "string",
  "latitudeInDb": "string",
  "longitudeInDb": "string",
  "location": "string",
  "countryCode": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "sccmFlag": true,
  "locationHint": "string"
}
```

A successful response returns code 204, meaning the IP address range is updated. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Deleting an IP Address Range

To delete an existing IP address range:

1. Send a `DELETE` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/v2/ipRanges/{ipRangeId}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/72057594037927936/v2/ipRanges/72057594038636775`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `ipRangeId`: The unique identifier of the IP address range.

A successful response returns code 200, meaning the IP address range is deleted. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Adding Field Descriptions

The following table includes available fields you can use for the IP address range API use cases:

| Field | Description | Required | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | Indicates if the IP address range is enabled (`true`) or disabled (`false`) | Yes | Default: `true` Boolean: `true`, `false` |
| ipRangeBegin | The beginning IP address range. The beginning IP address range must be less than the ending IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed. | Yes | String |
| ipRangeEnd | The ending IP address range. The ending IP address range must be greater than the beginning IP address range. The `subnetCidr` field is not required if `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are passed. | Yes | String |
| latitudeInDb | The latitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range | Yes | String |
| location | The location of the IP address range | Yes | String |
| locationHint | The location hint to be sent along with a Zscaler virtual IP address to Zscaler Client Connector if it is configured. This field is required if the `sccmFlag` field is set to `true`. | No | String |
| longitudeInDb | The longitude coordinate for the location of the IP address range | Yes | String |
| name | The name of the IP address range | Yes | String |
| sccmFlag | Indicates if the location hint is sent along with a Zscaler virtual IP address to Zscaler Client Connector if it is configured. If Zscaler Client Connector receives the location hint, Zscaler Client Connector creates a pseudo network adapter and applies the location hint to the name of the adapter for the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) location boundary. | Yes | Default: `false` Boolean: `true`, `false` |
| subnetCidr | The IP address subnet in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation used for server-to-client connectivity. The `ipRangeBegin` or `ipRangeEnd` fields are not required if `subnetCidr` is passed. | Yes | String |

## CSV User Attributes

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/csv-user-attributes
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Workflow Automation API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > CSV User Attributes
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T11:33Z

Zscaler Workflow Automation - DLP Incident Management API.

**Servers:** `https://api.us1.zsworkflow.net`

### `GET /dlp/v1/csv-user-data/{csv_user_data_uuid}/download`

Fetches a pre-signed AWS S3 bucket link to download your previously uploaded CSV file and the validation error file, depending on the parameter type.

- Operation ID: `getCsvUserDataDownloadUrl`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `csv_user_data_uuid` | path | yes | string(uuid) | The unique identifier (UUID) used to identify a specific user in the CSV file. |
| `type` | query | no | string | The type of the file that is downloaded. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

## Data Loss Prevention

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/data-loss-prevention
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Data Loss Prevention
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T07:06Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /cloudToCloudIR`

Retrieves the list of DLP Incident Receivers configured for Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding. Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding is configured in DLP policies, including Inline Web DLP, Endpoint DLP, Email DLP, and SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP policy rules. To learn more, see [Configure DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/dlp-cloud-cloud-incident-forwarding).

These Incident Receivers can be associated with Inline Web DLP and SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP rules via API by using the `/webDlpRules` and `/casbDlpRules` endpoints respectively.

- Operation ID: `C2CIncidentReceiverResource_getC2CIR`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | no | object | Specifies the page offset |
| `pageSize` | query | no | object | Specifies the page size |
| `search` | query | no | object | The search string used to match against the names of Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding tenants and their configurations |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /cloudToCloudIR/config/{id}/validateDelete`

Validates the specified cloud storage configuration (e.g., Amazon S3 bucket configuration) of a Cloud-to-Cloud DLP Incident Receiver by verifying the configuration's current association status with policy rules. Configurations cannot be deleted while being associated with policy rules.

- Operation ID: `C2CIncidentReceiverResource_validateConfigDelete`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | object | System-generated unique ID of a Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Receiver's storage configuration that must be validated for deletion. **Note**: The configuration ID can be obtained using the `GET /cloudToCloudIR` request. This value pertains to the cloud storage configuration ID returned within the `smirBucketConfig` object and not the tenant ID. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Successful Operation |

Retrieves the number of DLP Incident Receivers configured for Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding

`GET /cloudToCloudIR`

### `GET /dlpDictionaries/{dictId}/predefinedIdentifiers`

Retrieves the list of identifiers that are available for selection in the specified hierarchical DLP dictionary. This information can be obtained for predefined hierarchical dictionaries such as the Driver’s License (United States), Passport Number (European Union), and Credentials and Secrets dictionaries and their clones.

Each identifier represents a sub-dictionary that consists of specific patterns. The Driver’s License (United States) dictionary includes one sub-dictionary for each state in the United States and the District of Columbia. For example, the Driver's License (United States) dictionary includes one sub-dictionary for each state in the United States, and you can customize this dictionary to detect the driver's licenses issued by specific states (e.g., California, New York, and Texas) by selecting the respective sub-dictionary identifier.

To learn more about hierarchical dictionaries, see [Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-predefined-dlp-dictionaries).

- Operation ID: `DlpDictionaryResource_getPredefinedHierarchicalIdentifiersByDictionaryId`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dictId` | path | yes | object | The ID of the hierarchical DLP dictionary |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /dlpEngines`

Adds a new custom DLP engine. A DLP engine is a collection of one or more [DLP Dictionaries](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dlp-dictionaries), combined using logical operators. DLP engines can be used in DLP policies to detect specific content in the users' traffic. The Zscaler service provides predefined DLP engines and supports custom DLP engines. To learn more, see [About DLP Engines](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dlp-engines) and [Understanding DLP Engines](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-dlp-engines).

**Note**: To enable `/dlpEngines` endpoints that use POST, PUT, and DELETE methods for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

- Operation ID: `DlpEngineResource_addCustomDLPEngine`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | body | no | DlpEngineDom | Details of a custom DLP engine formed by combining DLP dictionaries using logical operators. To learn how to add custom DLP engines, see [Adding Custom DLP Engines](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-custom-dlp-engine). |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

Gets a name and ID dictionary for all DLP engines.

### `POST /dlpEngines/validateDlpExpr`

Validates the logical expression within a DLP engine that is formed by combining DLP dictionaries and provides error information if the expression is invalid. To learn more about DLP engine expressions, see [Understanding DLP Engines](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-dlp-engines).

**Note**: To enable `/dlpEngines` endpoints that use POST, PUT, and DELETE methods for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

- Operation ID: `DlpEngineResource_validateDlpPattern`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | body | no | string | Logical expression within a DLP engine formed by combining DLP dictionaries using operators. This parameter requires the input in a certain format. For example, an expression combining ABA Bank Routing Numbers and Credit Cards dictionaries using an AND operator with zero match count each would be ((D63.S > 0) AND (D38.S > 0)), where 63 is the ID of the Credit Cards dictionary and 38 is the ID of the ABA Bank Routing Numbers dictionary. The dictionary ID is wrapped around by a prefix (D) and a suffix (.S). Engine expression examples: `((D63.S > 1))`; `((D63.S > 1) AND (D38.S > 0))`; `((D63.S > 1) OR (D38.S > 0))`; `(D63.S > 0) AND ( NOT ( (D61.S > 0) ) ) )`; `(SUM(D63.S, D38.S) > 3)` In the preceding examples, 63 represents the ID of the Credit Cards dictionary, 61 is the Financial Statements dictionary ID, and 38 is the ABA Bank Routing Numbers dictionary ID. **Note**: Zscaler recommends validating DLP engine expressions by sending a POST request to `/dlpEngines/validateDlpExpr` before configuring a DLP engine. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /dlpExactDataMatchSchemas`

Exact Data Match (EDM) templates (or EDM schemas) allow the Zscaler service to identify a record from a structured data source that matches predefined criteria. Using the Index Tool, you can create an EDM template that allows you to define this criteria (i.e., define the tokens) for your data records by importing a CSV file. After the data is defined and submitted within the tool, you can then apply the EDM template to a custom DLP dictionary or engine. This endpoint gets the EDM templates for all Index Tools used by the organization. To learn more, see

[About Exact Data Match](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-exact-data-match)

and

[About the Index Tool](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-index-tool)

.

- Operation ID: `AdvancedDataProtectionSchemaResource_getSchemas`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |

### `GET /idmprofile`

Indexed Document Match (IDM) templates (or IDM profiles) allow you to fingerprint your organization’s critical documents that contain sensitive data. By fingerprinting and indexing your documents, you can create a document repository that the Zscaler service can use to identify completely or partially matching documents when evaluating outbound traffic against a DLP policy. Using the Index Tool, you can create an IDM template that allows you to upload and fingerprint your documents. After you create an IDM template, you can then apply it to a custom DLP dictionary. This endpoint gets all of the IDM templates for all Index Tools used by the organization. To learn more, see

[About Indexed Document Match](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-indexed-document-match)

and

[About the Index Tool](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-index-tool)

.

- Operation ID: `IdmProfileResource_getProfiles`

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/microtenants/{microtenantId}`

**Gets the given Microtenant details for the specified customer.**

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |

### `PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/microtenants/{microtenantId}`

**Updates the Microtenant details for the specified ID.**

- Operation ID: `updateScope`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `microtenantId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained in the API Keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations are limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → MicrotenantDto

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |

| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/legacy-apis/deleting-cloud-branch-connectors-using-api","lastmod":"2026-01-06T23:49Z","nid":"1447461"} -->
## Deleting Cloud & Branch Connectors Using API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/deleting-cloud-branch-connectors-using-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Working with APIs > Deleting Cloud & Branch Connectors Using API
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: Information on Deleting Cloud & Branch Connector use cases applicable to the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector cloud service API.

To delete Cloud and Branch Connectors using the Cloud & Branch Connector API, use the Cloud or Branch Connector group ID and the virtual machine (VM) ID of the Cloud or Branch Connector you want to delete.

Zscaler recommends that you shut down appliances before you delete them with the API. You can then verify that no mistakes were made when executing API calls (e.g., inadvertently deleting the wrong appliance). If you make a mistake, you can power the appliance back on and allow it to reregister. Once you’ve verified that the correct appliance has been deleted, you can remove the appliance from the cloud provider or hypervisor dashboard to complete the task.

- For Cloud Connectors: shutdown the Cloud Connector appliance in the AWS/Azure portal. When the appliance has been successfully deleted via the API, you can remove it from the AWS/Azure portal.
- For Branch Connectors: shutdown the Branch Connector appliance from the hypervisor dashboard (e.g., ESXi, KVM, etc.). When the appliance has been successfully deleted via the API, you can remove it from the hypervisor portal.

## Getting a List of Cloud & Branch Connector Groups

To get a list of Cloud & Branch Connector groups, send a GET request to `/ecgroup`. You can use the following optional parameters:

- `page`: Specify a page offset.
- `pageSize`: Specify the page length, up to a limit of 1000.

For example, in Python:

- Getting a List of Cloud & Branch Connector Groups (Python 3.x)

## Getting Details of a Specific Cloud or Branch Connector Group

To get information about a specific Cloud or Branch Connector group, send a GET request to `/ecgroup/{id}`, specifying the group ID (`id`) and optionally using the following parameters:

- `page`: Specify a page offset.
- `pageSize`: Specify the page length, up to a limit of 1000.

For example, in Python:

- Getting Details of a Specific Cloud or Branch Connector Group (Python 3.x)

## Getting Details of a Specific VM

To get information about a specific VM in a Cloud or Branch Connector group, send a GET request to `/ecgroup/{id}/vm/{vmid}`, specifying the group ID (`id`) and VM ID (`vmid`).

For example, in Python:

- Getting Details of a Specific VM (Python 3.x)

## Deleting a Specific VM

To delete a specific VM:

1. Send a DELETE request to `/ecgroup/{id}/vm/{vmid}`, specifying the group ID (`id`) and VM ID (`vmid`).
2. [Activate the changes to your configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/getting-started-api#activatingconfigurationchanges) by sending a PUT request to `/ecAdminActivateStatus/activate`.

For example, in Python:

- Deleting a Specific VM (Python 3.x)

## Verifying the Deletion of a Specific VM

To verify the deletion of a specific VM, send a GET request to `/ecgroup/{id}/vm/{vmid}`, specifying the group ID (`id`) and VM ID (`vmid`) of the deleted VM. If the deletion was successful, this request returns a [404 Not Found](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/api-response-codes-and-error-messages) status.

```
# Import Required Modules
import time, requests, json, urllib3, getpass

# Variables
cloudName = input("Cloud Name (e.g., zscloud.net): ")
username = input("Username: ")
password = getpass.getpass("Password: ")
apiKey = input("APIKey: ")

# Construct base URL
base_url = "https://connector." + cloudName + "/api/v1/"

# Obfuscate API Key
def obfuscateApiKey (apiKey):
   seed = apiKey
   now = int(time.time() * 1000)
   n = str(now)[-6:]
   r = str(int(n) >> 1).zfill(6)
   key = ""
   for i in range(0, len(str(n)), 1):
       key += seed[int(str(n)[i])]
   for j in range(0, len(str(r)), 1):
       key += seed[int(str(r)[j])+2]
   return key

headers = {'Content-Type':'application/json'}
urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)

# Create Session
def createSession(username, password, apiKey):
  auth_url = base_url + 'auth'
  now = int(time.time() * 1000)
  payload = {'apiKey':obfuscateApiKey(apiKey), 'username':username, 'password':password, 'timestamp':now  }
  s = requests.Session()
  # Added verify=False to bypass ZCC certificate otherwise call may fail with unable to verify SSL cert for certain cloud
  r = s.post(auth_url,data=json.dumps(payload),headers=headers, verify=False)
  return s

# Get Cloud & Branch Connector groups
def getConnectorGroup(s):
   ccgroup_url = base_url + 'ecgroup'
   list_of_ccgroups = s.get(ccgroup_url, headers=headers)
   return list_of_ccgroups.json()

f = createSession(username, password, apiKey)

# Print Connector Groups
print(getConnectorGroup(f))
```

# Import Required Modules
import time, requests, json, urllib3, getpass

# Variables
cloudName = input("Cloud Name (e.g., zscloud.net): ")
username = input("Username: ")
password = getpass.getpass("Password: ")
apiKey = input("APIKey: ")
ccGroupID = input("Enter the Cloud or Branch Connector Group ID: ")
vmID = input("Enter the VM ID of the Cloud or Branch Connector within the Group ID specified previously: ")

# Construct base URL
base_url = "https://connector." + cloudName + "/api/v1/"

# Obfuscate API Key
def obfuscateApiKey (apiKey):
   seed = apiKey
   now = int(time.time() * 1000)
   n = str(now)[-6:]
   r = str(int(n) >> 1).zfill(6)
   key = ""
   for i in range(0, len(str(n)), 1):
       key += seed[int(str(n)[i])]
   for j in range(0, len(str(r)), 1):
       key += seed[int(str(r)[j])+2]
   return key

headers = {'Content-Type':'application/json'}
urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)

# Create Session
def createSession(username, password, apiKey):
  auth_url = base_url + 'auth'
  now = int(time.time() * 1000)
  payload = {'apiKey':obfuscateApiKey(apiKey), 'username':username, 'password':password, 'timestamp':now  }
  s = requests.Session()
  # Added verify=False to bypass ZCC certificate otherwise call may fail with unable to verify SSL cert for certain cloud
  r = s.post(auth_url,data=json.dumps(payload),headers=headers, verify=False)
  return s

# Delete Cloud or Branch Connector VM
def deleteConnector(s):
   ccgroup_url = base_url + 'ecgroup/' + ccGroupID + '/vm/' + vmID
   list_of_ccgroups = s.delete(ccgroup_url, headers=headers)
   return list_of_ccgroups.json()

# Activate Changes
def activateChanges(s):
   activation_url = base_url + 'ecAdminActivateStatus/activate'
   activation_status = s.put(activation_url, headers=headers)
   return activation_status

f = createSession(username, password, apiKey)
delete_result = deleteConnector(f)

# Display deletion status
print("\nDeletion Status:")
print(delete_result)

# Display activation status
print("\nActivation Status:")
print(activateChanges(f).text)

## Device Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/device-groups
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Device Groups
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /deviceGroups`

Gets a list of device groups.

- Operation ID: `DeviceGroupResource_getDeviceGroups`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeDeviceInfo` | query | no | object | Include or exclude device information. |
| `includePseudoGroups` | query | no | object | Include or exclude Zscaler Client Connector and Cloud Browser Isolation-related device groups. |
| `includeIOTGroups` | query | no | object | Include or exclude IoT device groups. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /deviceGroups/devices`

Gets a list of devices. Any given search parameters are applied during device search. Search parameters are based on device name, model, owner, OS type, and OS version. The devices listed can also be restricted to return information only for ones belonging to specific users.

- Operation ID: `DeviceGroupResource_getDevices`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | query | no | object | The device group name. |
| `model` | query | no | object | The device models. |
| `owner` | query | no | object | The device owners. |
| `osType` | query | no | object | The device's operating system. |
| `osVersion` | query | no | object | The device's operating system version. |
| `deviceGroupId` | query | no | object | The unique identifier for the device group. |
| `userIds` | query | no | object | Used to list devices for specific users. |
| `search_all` | query | no | object | Used to match against all device attribute information. |
| `includeAll` | query | no | object | Used to include or exclude Cloud Browser Isolation devices. |
| `page` | query | no | object | Specifies the page offset. |
| `pageSize` | query | no | object | Specifies the page size. The default size is 100, but the maximum size is 1000. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /deviceGroups/devices/lite`

Gets a list of devices that includes device ID, name, and owner name. Any given search parameters are applied during device search. Search parameters are based on device or user name and owner. The devices listed can also be restricted to return information only for ones belonging to specific users.

- Operation ID: `DeviceGroupResource_getDevicesLite`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | query | no | object | The device group name. |
| `userIds` | query | no | object | Used to list devices for specific users. |
| `includeAll` | query | no | object | Used to include or exclude Cloud Browser Isolation devices. |
| `page` | query | no | object | Specifies the page offset. |
| `pageSize` | query | no | object | Specifies the page size. The default size is 100, but the maximum size is 1000. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

Zscaler Workflow Automation - DLP Incident Management API.

**Servers:** `https://api.us1.zsworkflow.net`

### `GET /dlp/v1/incidents/transactions/{transactionId}`

Gets the list of all DLP incidents associated with the transaction ID. A transaction ID can contain one or more DLP incidents.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transactionId` | path | yes | string | The ID of the transaction that violated the DLP rules. |

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |
| 500 | Failed to process the request |

Deletes the DLP incident for the specified incident ID.

- Operation ID: `deleteDLPIncident`

| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

Filters a list of DLP incident groups to which the specified incident ID belongs.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

### `POST /dlp/v1/incidents/{dlpIncidentId}/close`

Updates the status of the incident to resolved and closes the incident with a resolution label and a resolution code.

- Operation ID: `closeDLPIncident`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dlpIncidentId` | path | yes | string | The ID of the incident. |

| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

### `POST /dlp/v1/incidents/{dlpIncidentId}/notes`

Adds notes to the incident during updates or status changes.

- Operation ID: `addNoteDLPIncident`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dlpIncidentId` | path | yes | string | The ID of the incident for which the note is added. |

Assign lables (a label name and it's associated value) to DLP incidents.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dlpIncidentId` | path | yes | string | The ID of DLP incident to which the label is assigned. |

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

### `POST /dlp/v1/incidents/search`

Filters DLP incidents based on the given time range and the field values. The supported field values are:

- Severity
- Priority
- Transaction ID
- Status
- Source
- Source DLP Type
- Labels
- Incident Group
- Engine

The supported time range values are:

- Start date and time
- End date and time

- Operation ID: `searchDLPIncidents`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | no | integer | Specifies the page number of the incident in a multi-paginated response. This field is not required if page ID field is used. |
| `pageSize` | query | no | integer | Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page). The maximum page size is 100. |
| `pageId` | query | no | string | Specifies the page ID of the incident in a multi-paginated response. It is a unique identifier returned in the first search request. The page ID can be used instead of the page number in subsequent search requests for faster and more efficient results. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → SearchRequestFilters

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 500 | Failed to process the request |

### `GET /dlp/v1/incidents/{dlpIncidentId}/triggers`

Downloads the actual data that triggered the incident.

- Operation ID: `getDLPIncidentTrigger`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dlpIncidentId` | path | yes | string | The ID of the incident for which the trigger data is downloaded. |
| `fetchTriggerContext` | query | no | boolean | (Optional) Specifies whether to download the complete incident trigger data, including the prefix and suffix information. Set this field to `true` to fetch the prefix and suffix data.The default value is `false`. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |

### `GET /dlp/v1/incidents/{dlpIncidentId}/evidence`

Gets the evidence URL of the incident. The evidence link can be used to view and download the XML file with the actual data that triggered the incident.

- Operation ID: `getDLPIncidentEvidenceMetadata`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dlpIncidentId` | path | yes | string | The ID of the incident for which evidence URL is fetched. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |

| 404 | Resource does not exist |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api","lastmod":"2026-05-17T07:06Z","nid":"1400431"} -->
## Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Working with APIs > Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API
- Last modified: 2026-05-17T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on admin audit log and event log use cases applicable to the cloud service API supported by Internet & SaaS (ZIA).

This article provides information on how to generate and download audit log and event log reports as CSV files using the API.

## Audit Logs

Audit logs record all admin activities in the Zscaler Admin Console for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and the actions performed using the API. You can download admin audit log reports for up to 31 days or a maximum of 1,000 records at a time. Admin audit logs are stored for the last 6 months. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-audit-logs).

The following steps explain how to generate and download an admin audit log report using the API:

- 1. Generate the report.
- 2. Poll for report status.
- 3. Download the report.

## Event Logs

Event logs track all recorded SCIM client activity, such as creating, updating, deleting, and other actions performed on user and group accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console for Internet & SaaS. To learn more, see [About Event Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-event-logs).

The following steps explain how to generate and download an event log report using the API:

- 1. Generate the report.
- 2. Poll for report status.
- 3. Download the report.

1. Initiate the audit log report generation by sending a POST request to `/auditlogEntryReport` with the date range specified in the request Body: For example, in Python: `payload = { "startTime":1493967600000, "endTime":1496645999999 }`The request Body can include additional parameters to filter specific records based on predefined criteria. You can also paginate the results. To learn more, see the [API Reference](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/admin-audit-logs). This POST request returns a status ID for the report being created along with other information. Sample response: `{ "status" : "EXECUTING", "statusId" : "eaab786c44674a96be790625f527b0e9", "reportType" : "ZMANAGE_AUDIT_LOG_ENTRY_REPORT", }`
  - `startTime`: The start time (Unix timestamp in milliseconds) in a specific time frame to be used for report generation.
  - `endTime`: The end time (Unix timestamp in milliseconds) in a specific time frame to be used for report generation.
2. From the `POST /auditlogEntryReport` response, capture the `statusId` value (e.g., "`eaab786c44674a96be790625f527b0e9`"). The `statusId` is required in subsequent requests to poll for the report status and then to download the report.

After initiating the report generation, poll for the report status by making repeated requests to `GET /auditlogEntryReport` and appending the `statusId` query parameter received from the POST response (i.e., `GET /auditlogEntryReport?statusId=eaab786c44674a96be790625f527b0e9`).

Sample response:

```
{
 "status" : "EXECUTING",
 "progressItemsComplete" : 0,
 "progressEndTime" : 0,
 "percentage" : 0
}
```

Continue polling until the report reaches a terminal status, such as `COMPLETE`, `CANCELLED`, `ERRORED`, or `STOP`.

Sample response:

```
{
 "status" : "COMPLETE",
 "progressItemsComplete" : 0,
 "progressEndTime" : 0,
 "percentage" : 0
}
```

When the status is `COMPLETE`, you can download the report as a CSV file by sending a GET request to `/auditlogEntryReport/download` and appending the `statusId` query parameter received from the POST response (i.e., `GET /auditlogEntryReport/download?statusId=eaab786c44674a96be790625f527b0e9`). A successful response returns a `200 OK` status code with the log data available in the report.

Sample response:

```
Administrator,admin@acme.com
Report Created,"26 Mar 2026 04:07:28, PDT"
Start Time,"25 Mar 2026 11:30:00, PDT"
End Time,"26 Mar 2026 04:02:38, PDT"
Time,User,Action,AA in Cloud,Result,Client IP,Interface,Category,Subcategory,Resource,Pre Action,After,TraceId
"26 Mar 2026 00:30:19, PDT",admin@acme.com,Sign In,zscalerbeta.net,Successful,192.0.2.1,API,Login,Login,,,,,
"26 Mar 2026 00:23:42, PDT",admin@acme.com,Sign In,zscalerbeta.net,Successful,192.0.2.2,UI,Login,Login,,,,,
...
```

The response is formatted according to the time zone configured in the Zscaler Admin Console under **Account Settings** icon > **Account Settings** in the top navigation bar. To learn more, see [Customizing Your Account Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/customizing-your-account-settings).

- You can download only the latest report generated at any time. Making a `POST /auditlogEntryReport` request overwrites any previously generated report.
- To cancel a report generation request, send a DELETE request to `/auditlogEntryReport` with the `statusId` query parameter retrieved from the POST response.

1. Initiate the event log report generation by sending a POST request to `/eventlogEntryReport` with the date range specified in the request Body: For example, in Python: `payload = { "startTime":1493967600000, "endTime":1496645999999 }`The request Body can include additional parameters to filter specific records based on predefined criteria. You can also paginate the results. To learn more, see the [API Reference](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/event-logs). This POST request returns a status ID for the report being created along with other information. Sample response: `{ "status" : "EXECUTING", "statusId" : "eaab786c44674a96be790625e347a1d8", "reportType" : "ZMANAGE_EVENT_LOG_ENTRY_REPORT", }`
  - `startTime`: The start time (Unix timestamp in milliseconds) in a specific time frame to be used for report generation.
  - `endTime`: The end time (Unix timestamp in milliseconds) in a specific time frame to be used for report generation.
2. From the `POST /eventlogEntryReport` response, capture the `statusId` value (e.g., "`eaab786c44674a96be790625e347a1d8`"). The `statusId` is required in subsequent requests to poll for the report status and then to download the report.

After initiating the report generation, poll for the report status by making repeated requests to `GET /eventlogEntryReport` and appending the `statusId` query parameter received from the POST response (i.e., `GET /eventlogEntryReport?statusId=eaab786c44674a96be790625e347a1d8`).

Sample response:

```
{
 "status" : "EXECUTING",
 "progressItemsComplete" : 0,
 "progressEndTime" : 0,
 "percentage" : 0
}
```

Continue polling until the report reaches a terminal status, such as `COMPLETE`, `CANCELLED`, `ERRORED`, or `STOP`.

Sample response:

```
{
 "status" : "COMPLETE",
 "progressItemsComplete" : 0,
 "progressEndTime" : 0,
 "percentage" : 0
}
```

When the status is `COMPLETE`, you can download the report as a CSV file by sending a GET request to `/eventlogEntryReport/download` and appending the `statusId` query parameter received from the POST response (i.e., `GET /eventlogEntryReport/download?statusId=eaab786c44674a96be790625e347a1d8`). A successful response returns a `200 OK` status code with the log data available in the report.

Sample response:

```
Administrator,techpubs@safemarch.com
Report Created,"26 Mar 2026 04:24:59, PDT"
Start Time,"25 Mar 2026 17:00:00, PDT"
End Time,"26 Mar 2026 04:24:57, PDT"
Time,Category,SUBCATEGORY,Result,Message,Error Code,Status Code,Pre Action,After
...
```

The response is formatted according to the time zone configured in the Zscaler Admin Console under **Account Settings** icon > **Account Settings** in the top navigation bar. To learn more, see [Customizing Your Account Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/customizing-your-account-settings).

- You can download only the latest report generated at any time. Making a `POST /eventlogEntryReport` request overwrites any previously generated report.
- To cancel a report generation request, send a DELETE request to `/eventlogEntryReport` with the `statusId` query parameter retrieved from the POST response.

.

| Code | Description |

Updates browser-based end user notification (EUN) configuration details. To learn more, see

.

| 200 | Successful Operation |

Retrieves the list of notification templates for browser-based and Zscaler Client Connector-based notifications by policy type. To learn more, see

[About Browser EUN Template](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-browser-eun-template)

and

[About Zscaler Client Connector-Based End User Notifications](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-zscaler-client-connector-based-end-user-notifications)

.

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

Retrieves the EUN enablement status for the specified notification type

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| --- | --- |

.

Setting false retrieves a different set of file types available when DLP engines are not used. |

To access detailed ZPA API documentation, including references and use cases, refer to the [Zscaler Help Portal](/zpa/about-zpa-api).

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/{customerId}/enrollmentCert`

**Gets all configured enrollment certificate details for the specified customer.**

- Operation ID: `getAllSigningCert`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `search` | query | no | string | The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API. |
| `pagesize` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500. |
| `page` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page number. |

## Event Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/event-logs
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Event Logs
- Last modified: 2026-03-26T22:44Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /auditlogEntryReport`

Retrieves the audit log report generation status based on the specified report status ID (retrieved from POST `/auditlogEntryReport` response). You need to continue polling for the report status until a terminal status is reached (e.g., `COMPLETE`) to download the report subsequently.

To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `getAuditReportEntryCsvExportStatus`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /auditlogEntryReport`

Generates an audit log report for the specified time period. The report includes audit information for every call made to the cloud service API during the specified time period. Creating a new audit log report overwrites a previously generated report.

After making this POST request, you need to poll for the report status by sending GET requests to `/auditlogEntryReport` along with the status ID obtained from the POST request. Continue polling until the report reaches a terminal status (e.g., `COMPLETE` or `CANCELLED`). When the status is `COMPLETE`, you can download the report as a CSV file by sending a GET request to `/auditlogEntryReport/download`. To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `startAuditReportEntryCsvExport`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | body | no | AuditLogEntryRequest | Criteria used for generating the audit log report, such as time range, filters, pagination, etc. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-audit-logs). |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `DELETE /auditlogEntryReport`

Cancels the request previously made to create an audit log report

- Operation ID: `cancelAuditReportEntryCsvExport`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /auditlogEntryReport/download`

Downloads the most recently created audit log report based on the specified report status ID.

Before sending this request, ensure that you generate a report using `POST /auditlogEntryReport` and poll for report status using `GET /auditlogEntryReport` until the status indicates the report is completed (i.e., status is `COMPLETE`). To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `getAuditReportEntryCsvData`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /eventlogEntryReport`

Retrieves the event log report generation status based on the specified report status ID (retrieved from POST `/eventlogEntryReport` response). You need to continue polling for the report status until a terminal status is reached (e.g., `COMPLETE`) to download the report subsequently.

To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `EventLogEntryReportResource_getEventReportEntryCsvExportStatus`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /eventlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /eventlogEntryReport`

Generates an event log report for the specified time period. Creating a new event log report overwrites a previously generated report.

After making this POST request, you need to poll for the report status by sending GET requests to `/eventlogEntryReport` along with the status ID obtained from the POST request. Continue polling until the report reaches a terminal status (e.g., `COMPLETE` or `CANCELLED`). When the status is `COMPLETE`, you can download the report as a CSV file by sending a GET request to `/eventlogEntryReport/download`. To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

**Responses:**

## Federate Applications

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/federate-applications
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Federate Applications
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T10:46Z

To access detailed ZPA API documentation, including references and use cases, refer to the [Zscaler Help Portal](/zpa/about-zpa-api).

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/customers/{customerId}/application/host/{host_id}`

Gets the federated applications for the specified customer using filters (i.e., application host ID, domain names, and enabled status).

- Operation ID: `getFederatedApplicationsFromHost`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |
| `host_id` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The application segment ID from the host partner. This is the `partnerGid` value returned when getting active federated partners. |
| `search` | query | no | string | The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API. |
| `page` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page number. |
| `pagesize` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |

### `PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/customers/{customerId}/application/federate`

Federates an existing application segment from a host partner with one or more guest partners.

- Operation ID: `federateApplication`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → ApplicationFederationRequest

## Federating Applications Using API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/federating-applications-using-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Working with APIs > Federating Applications Using API
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T10:41Z
- Summary: Information on federating business partner federation use cases applicable to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) cloud service API.

This article provides information on Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) application federation use cases using APIs. All APIs are rate limited. To learn more, see [Understanding Rate Limiting](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-rate-limiting), [Federating Defined Application Segments](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/federating-defined-application-segments), and [Understanding Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-business-business-b2b-federation).

## Getting a List of Federated Applications from the Host Partner

To get a list of federated applications shared by the specified host partner by filtering, sorting, and pagination:

1. Send a `GET` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/customers/{customerId}/application/host/{host_id}?microtenantId={microtenantId}&page=1&pagesize=20&search=<search>`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/customers/72057595111669760/application/host/145260601092866519?page=1&pagesize=20&scopeId=145260601092866314&search=enabled%20EQ%20true`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `host_id`: The application segment ID from the host partner. This is the `partnerGid` value returned when [getting active federated partners](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/federating-partners-using-api#getActiveFederatedPartners).
  - Valid search string values. The search string values are in the format `fieldName operator fieldValue`. Only search string values that correspond to the values for valid fields and filters are supported. For example, the string `enabled%20EQ%20true` is supported for the **Enabled** filter, using the **Equals (EQ)** operator, for the true filter value.
  - `microtenantId`: The unique identifier of the Microtenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the `microtenantId` field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The `microtenantId` can be obtained from the [API Keys](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-api-key-management) page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass `microtenantId` as `0` when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the `microtenantId` is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. To learn more, see [Configuring Microtenants Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-microtenants-using-api).

The endpoint to get a list of federated applications shared by the host partner is used by the host partner to view what is already shared, or by a guest partner when called against a `host_id` they have visibility into to view what was shared with them.

- View an example response.

```
{
  "totalPages": "1",
  "totalCount": "1",
  "list": [
    {
      "id": 145260601092866990,
      "name": "rdp-internal-host.com",
      "domainNames": [
        "rdp-internal-host.com"
      ],
      "tcpPortRanges": [3389, 3389],
      "udpPortRanges": [],
      "hostInfo": {
        "partnerGid": 72057595111669760,
        "partnerName": "Acme Corp",
        "partnerScopeName": "Default",
        "approvalStatus": "APPROVED",
        "federationStatus": "ACTIVE"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

A successful response returns code 204. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Federating an Application with Guest Partners

To federate an existing application segment from a host partner with one or more guest partners:

1. Send a `PUT` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/customers/{customerId}/application/federate?microtenantId={microtenantId}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/customers/72057595111669760/application/federate?microtenantId=145260601092866314`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `microtenantId`: The unique identifier of the Microtenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the `microtenantId` field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The `microtenantId` can be obtained from the [API Keys](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-api-key-management) page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass `microtenantId` as `0` when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the `microtenantId` is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. To learn more, see [Configuring Microtenants Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-microtenants-using-api).
3. Include the request headers to provide information about the request context:
  - Content-Type: `application/json`
  - Authorization: `Bearer <access_token>`
4. Provide the following JSON payload and include the following details:
  - `applicationGid`: The GID of the host application segment that you want to federate. To learn more, see Getting a List of Federated Applications from the Host Partner.
  - `guestGid`: The list of guest partner GIDs to share the application with. This array must be the partners the host has an active federation with. To learn more, see [Federating Partners Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/federating-partners-using-api).

- View the minimum criteria JSON payload.

```
{
  "applicationGid": 0,
  "guestGids": [
    0
  ]
}
```

- View an example JSON payload.

```
{
  "applicationGid": 145260601092866519,
  "guestGids": [
    72057595111669761,
    72057595111669762
  ]
}
```

A successful response returns code 204. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

## Field Descriptions

The following table includes descriptions of available fields you can use for the federating applications use cases:

| Field | Description | Required | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| customerId | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant | Yes | Integer |
| host_id | The application segment ID from the host partner. This is the `partnerGid` value returned when [getting active federated partners](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/federating-partners-using-api#getActiveFederatedPartners). | Yes | Integer |
| microtenantId | The unique identifier of the Microtenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the `microtenantId` field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The `microtenantId` can be obtained from the [API Keys](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-api-key-management) page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass `microtenantId` as `0` when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the `microtenantId` is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. To learn more, see [Configuring Microtenants Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-microtenants-using-api). | No | Integer |
| search | The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API | No | String For example: `guestGid EQ 123`; `enabled EQ true`; `domainNames CONTAINS example.com` |
| page | Specifies the page number | No | Integer This field is `1` by default. |
| pagesize | Specifies the page size | No | Integer If not provided, the default page size is `20`. The maximum page size is `500`. |

## Fetching URL Filtering Rules Using Pagination and Search Filters

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/fetching-url-filtering-rules-using-pagination-and-search-filters
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Working with APIs > Fetching URL Filtering Rules Using Pagination and Search Filters
- Last modified: 2026-02-17T06:06Z
- Summary: Use case on how to fetch URL Filtering rules applying pagination and search filters using the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) cloud service API.

The URL Filtering policy cloud service API allows you to retrieve all URL Filtering rules and use server-side search filters to refine the query results. The URL Filtering policy cloud service API supports pagination and filtering parameters, allowing users to manage large sets of URL Filtering rules.

## Fetching URL Filtering Rules

To retrieve all URL Filtering rules, you must iterate through the paginated results returned by the API. To do this, you must first get the total rule count, then loop through the pages, making a`GET`request for each page:

1. Get the total number of rules: Before fetching the rules, make a call using the `GET /urlFilteringRules/count` endpoint to determine the total number of existing rules.
2. Loop through the pages: After obtaining the total rule count, calculate the total number of pages required by dividing the total count by page size. `(totalPages = ceil (total count / page size)` You must then loop from page `1` to `total pages`, making a `GET` request for each page.

Here's a pseudocode example:

```
pageSize = 100 // Or any desired size up to a max limit
totalRulesCount = GET "/urlFilteringRules/count"
totalPages = ceil(totalRulesCount / pageSize)
allRules = []
for page in 1..totalPages:
rulesPage = GET "/urlFilteringRules?page=" + page + "&pageSize=" + pageSize
allRules.append(rulesPage)
// The 'allRules' array now contains the complete ruleset
```

## Leveraging Server-Side Search

Pagination can be combined with server-side search filters to efficiently retrieve specific sets of URL Filtering rules. Filters can be applied using query parameters such as `name`, `location`, or other supported fields.

For example:

- To retrieve all URL Filtering rules with "Finance" in the name field and on the second page, configure the request to `GET /urlFilteringRules?name=Finance&page=2&pageSize=100`.
- To get the count of all rules assigned to the "Headquarters" location, configure the request to `GET /urlFilteringRules/count?locations=Headquarters`.

## Firewall Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/firewall-policies
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Firewall Policies
- Last modified: 2026-07-27T07:06Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /firewallFilteringRules`

Retrieves all rules in the Firewall Filtering policy

**Note**: The API response captures all updates made to the Firewall Filtering rules directly (i.e., action performed directly on the rule by admin or API client) or incidentally as a result of other rule modifications (e.g., a higher-order rule creation automatically modifies the rule order for existing rules with lower order). The `lastModifiedBy` and `lastModifiedTime` fields of a rule correspond strictly to the latest change to the rule or the rule set. For example, when a new rule of order 1 is added, an existing rule with order 1 shifts down to order 2 and this change applies to the remaining rules. In this case, the `lastModifiedBy` and `lastModifiedTime` fields for all rules correspond to the admin or API client who created the new rule and the time it was created.

However, when you use audit logs to view the change records logged for admins and API clients, the incidental rule changes are excluded from the audit logs. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-audit-logs).

- Operation ID: `FirewallFilteringRulesResource_getFirewallFilteringRules`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ruleName` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule names using specified keywords |
| `ruleLabel` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule labels using specified keywords |
| `ruleLabelId` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule label IDs using specified keywords |
| `ruleOrder` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule order using specified keywords |
| `ruleDescription` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule description using specified keywords |
| `ruleAction` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on rule actions using specified keywords |
| `location` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on locations using specified keywords |

| `user` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on users using specified keywords |
| `device` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on devices using specified keywords |
| `deviceGroup` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on device groups using specified keywords |
| `deviceTrustLevel` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on device trust levels using specified keywords |
| `srcIps` | query | no | object | Filters rules based on source IP addresses using specified keywords |

## Getting Started

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/getting-started
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Microsegmentation API > Getting Started
- Last modified: 2026-02-07T06:06Z
- Summary: Overview on the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) microsegmentation, that uses identity-based, least-privilege policies to control workload-to-workload communication, reduce lateral movement, and enforce Zero Trust.

Zscaler Microsegmentation APIs enable customers and partners to visualize and manage workload traffic flows within private applications, apply fine-grained segmentation, and query operational telemetry. The platform uses the Zscaler cloud and deployed agents to collect application flow data, enforce identity-based access policies, and monitor agent and system health.

### API Workflow Overview

To authenticate and make calls to the Microsegmentation API, you must complete the following steps:

- Ensure that all [prerequisites](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-zscaler-microsegmentation-api#prerequisites) are met.
- Set up [authentication using Postman](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-zscaler-microsegmentation-api#postman-authentication).
- [Configure a User-Agent header](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-zscaler-microsegmentation-api#user-agent-header).
- [Download the GraphQL Schema](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-graphql-schema-postman) in Postman and use it to make API calls.

## Getting Started

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/getting-started-client-connector-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Zscaler Client Connector API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Getting Started
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: To supply prerequisite information for access to the Zscaler Client Connector API.

Your organization must meet the following prerequisites before you can access the [Zscaler Client Connector API](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/understanding-zscaler-client-connector-api):

- You must enable the API for your organization. To enable the API, contact Zscaler Support or submit a Zscaler Support ticket.
- [Add an API key](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/adding-api-key).

If you need to obtain API keys, authenticate into, and make calls using [Zscaler OneAPI](https://help.zscaler.com/oneapi) endpoints, see [About API Clients](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/about-api-clients) in Authentication Service and [Getting Started](https://help.zscaler.com/oneapi/getting-started) with OneAPI.

After these prerequisites are met, you can:

- Locate your base URI
- Authenticate and create an API session
- Make an API call

To learn more about rate limits and HTTP status codes, see [Understanding Rate Limiting](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/understanding-rate-limiting) and [About Error Codes](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/about-error-codes). If you encounter any issues with the API, contact Zscaler Support.

The base URI for the API is `/public/v1` for the following:

- The endpoint to get a one-time password (OTP).
- The endpoint to get all passwords in the app profiles.
- The endpoint to get device details.
- The endpoint to remove devices from the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.

To learn more, see [Zscaler Client Connector API Reference Guide](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/zscaler-client-connector-api/api-developer-reference-guide/reference-guide).

Before executing any API calls, you must first authenticate via the API. Send a `POST` request to the `/login` endpoint with the following parameters:

- `apiKey`: A string that contains the API client ID. To learn more, see [About API Key Management](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/about-api-key-management).
- `secretKey`: A string that contains the client secret. The client secret is only available to copy when [adding an API key](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/adding-api-key).

Before making any API calls, you must retrieve your authorization token (`JWT Token<jwtToken>`). The authorization token is passed onto subsequent calls for authentication.

To authenticate via the API, use the following Python script to sign in and get the `JWT Token<jwtToken>`. In your script, enter the actual API key and actual secret key. These are highlighted in red.

```
import requests
url = "https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/auth/v1/login"
payload={"apiKey":"
{apiKey}
","secretKey":"
{secretKey}
"}
headers = {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json'
          }
response = requests.request("POST", url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(response.text)
```

Example `POST` request for sign-in using a Python script:

```
import requests
url = "https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/auth/v1/login"
payload={"apiKey":"b26j87u0-51n5-4th3-p278-m2b6usl9ca11","secretKey":"42bjp311-51j8-4s61-95jx-n7bbx10e5130"}
headers = {
          'Content-type': 'application/json'
          }
response = requests.request("POST", url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(response.text)
```

The client secret (i.e., secret key) is only accessible within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal when the API key is created for the first time. Ensure to copy your client secret to the clipboard when you first create your API key. The authentication token expiry time is set to 3600 seconds (one hour) by default.

- View an example response.

```
{
  "jwtToken" : "eyJraWQiOiI0bzZFS1k4STFqS1kwN2tQdjlqWV9",
  "message" : null
}
```

After you have your authorization token, you can make an API call. Send a `GET` request to the `/getOtp` endpoint to get a one-time password for a specific device.

Use the following Python script to get a one-time password. In your script, enter the actual Unique Device Identifier (UDID) and JWT token. These are highlighted in red.

```
import requests 
url = "https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/public/v1/getOtp?udid=
{udid}
" 
headers = { 
  "auth-token":"
{jwtToken}
" 
} 
response = requests.request("GET", url, headers=headers) 
print(response.text)
```

Example `GET` request to get the OTP using a Python script:

```
import requests
url = "https://mobile.<cloudName>.net/papi/public/v1/getOtp?udid=253B446D-D4A2-1F3E-DFAC-A51EDA415A55:705"
headers = {
  "auth-token":"eyJraWQiOiI0bzZFS1k4STFqS1kwN2tQdjlqWV9"
}
response = requests.request("GET", url, headers=headers)
print(response.text)
```

- View an example response.

When making API calls, consider the following best practices:

- Use UTF-8 encoding for all endpoints (e.g., use the `encodeUriComponent()` function in JavaScript to encode to UTF-8).
- When updating a resource, always send a `GET` request before the `PUT` or `POST`request. This retrieves the current values for the resource before you update the entire resource with new values. After the update, the next `GET` request for that resource returns the new values. By using this practice, you avoid potentially missing updates between `GET` and `PUT` or `POST` calls.
- Prevent API call caching by adding a dummy argument with a randomly generated number to all URL request strings. For example: `GET /getOtp?_=123456`?
- Create a dedicated user for each script. Don't use the same keys in multiple scripts that are running concurrently.

```
{
  "otp" : "kg08abdcp1"
}
```
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
